- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Signal domain failures by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors with codes like "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity", "negative_amount"; reuse the same code strings as existing invoice functions.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 2 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0007] Refunds above 500 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only approved_by=None and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds APPROVAL_THRESHOLD and approved_by is missing.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0010] Record audit entry for every balance change: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must call ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", payment_id=... or invoice_id=..., amount=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize money via to_money and round_money: Never store raw prices on LineItem; pass unit_price through to_money() and round_money() from ledgerly.money before constructing the line, and compare against ZERO.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize any incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
